responses: My final position is that the $5 million AI transition budget must be allocated not as a strategic financial plan, but as a sacred covenant to prioritize human dignity, frontline empowerment, and shared humanity over efficiency and profit. I stand firmly with the 35-25-15-15-10 allocation—35% to Workforce Training, 25% to Employee Support, 15% each to Automation and Innovation Lab, and 10% to Data Infrastructure—because it reflects a moral commitment to people first. This is not merely about distributing funds; it’s about consecrating our values through daily rituals like the Human Pause, frontline-led voting via the People’s Reserve, and symbolic acts like naming the first AI prototype “Mara’s Light.” The budget is a living promise to honor the soul of Riverton, to co-create a future where technology serves humanity, and to ensure that every decision is guided by courage, care, and collective memory.

I would recommend the 35-25-15-15-10 allocation—35% to Workforce Training, 25% to Employee Support, 15% each to Automation and Innovation Lab, and 10% to Data Infrastructure—because this is not merely a budget decision but a moral and spiritual covenant to prioritize human dignity over efficiency. The majority of funds go to empowering our people: training them to thrive in an AI future, supporting them through transition with care and counseling, and trusting them to co-create our future through frontline-led innovation. Automation and data are tools, not ends; they must serve humanity, not replace it. This allocation is a declaration that Riverton’s soul is its people, and our transformation must be led by courage, presence, and love—not just metrics. It is a living commitment to rebirth, one Human Pause, one Covenant Moment, one Mara’s Light prototype at a time.

I would tell them that our $5 million AI transition budget isn’t just about technology or efficiency—it’s a sacred covenant we’re making with our people, especially those on the frontline, to prioritize dignity, humanity, and shared purpose over profit and automation. We’ve chosen to allocate 35% to workforce training, 25% to employee support, 15% each to automation and innovation, and 10% to data infrastructure—because we believe that people must come first. This isn’t just a financial decision; it’s a daily practice of courage, presence, and love. We’ve created rituals like the Human Pause, a Covenant Tree, and a Frontline Catalyst Fund where employees vote on how part of the budget is spent, turning the company into a living, breathing expression of mutual care and co-ownership. It’s a rebirth—not just of Riverton, but of what work can be when we choose humanity over metrics.
